name: Hold non-critical alerts during quiet hours and send a digest

parameters.content:
### How it works
This workflow helps small teams and on-call operators take incoming alerts without being woken for every non-critical event. A webhook accepts a JSON payload. The workflow checks that a title or message is present, builds a fingerprint, and ignores repeats inside a configurable time window. It then uses your timezone and the alert severity. Critical alerts are sent immediately. Other alerts that arrive during quiet hours are held in workflow static data. A schedule trigger runs on an interval and, once quiet hours have ended, sends one digest that lists the held alerts and then clears those items. If the notification request fails after retries, the execution records the failure in the run output.

### Setup
Before you activate the workflow, open Receive Alert and add header authentication. The webhook is unauthenticated until you do this. In Load Settings, replace the alert_url placeholder https://example.invalid/your-alert-webhook with an HTTPS URL that accepts a JSON POST. Set timezone, quiet_start, quiet_end, critical_severities, and dedupe_window_minutes. Test a non-critical alert during quiet hours, a critical alert, a flush after quiet hours, and a repeated payload inside the dedupe window.

### Customization
Change the quiet window and the severities that bypass it. Adjust the flush interval so it is shorter than your quiet window. You can add a spreadsheet or database node after the result nodes for a durable log. Workflow static data stays on this n8n instance and is cleared if the instance is reset, so treat the buffer as short-term storage only.

## Receive and settings
The webhook and the flush schedule both use Load Settings. Replace the placeholder alert URL and set timezone and quiet hours there before you activate the workflow.

## Classify and hold
This section validates the payload, drops recent duplicates, holds non-critical alerts during quiet hours, and lets critical alerts through immediately.

## Notify and log
A JSON POST goes to your alert URL, with retries on failure. The result nodes write a structured outcome in the execution output so you can see what happened.

## Flush after quiet hours
The schedule trigger inspects the buffer after quiet hours end. If anything was held, it sends one digest and then clears those items.

Replace alert_url in Load Settings with your HTTPS endpoint before you activate this workflow. The example.invalid placeholder will not deliver alerts. Also add header authentication on Receive Alert; the webhook is open until you do.
